_about: Second paragraph of each home's text (the first is short_description in properties.json), written from the agency listing and in the site's plain tone. Facts only from the listing; French words are kept where the listing uses them (the glossary explains them). Nothing is generated from the record any more.

paragraphs.pepieux-stone-house-1962:
This village house was built in 1850 and was originally part of a château. It keeps its original features: a water pump, exposed beams and decorative roof tiles. It has been tastefully refitted and feels like a French country cottage.
Downstairs there is a large living room and kitchen in one, with a fully equipped kitchen that opens onto the living space. There are two bedrooms and two bathrooms, and two more rooms, one of which is used as a spare bedroom.
It is a low-maintenance house, a good second home or holiday rental in the Minervois.
paragraphs.le-vigeant-village-house-a37509:
The house is tucked away on a residents-only street, a short walk downhill to the River Vienne.
Downstairs, the living room opens into a spacious, light-filled kitchen and dining room with views over the private courtyard. Upstairs there are two bedrooms and a bathroom, and the front bedroom is especially large, with space for several beds.
An attached stone outbuilding (a dépendance), reached from the kitchen, gives plenty of storage and leads out to the courtyard. From the courtyard, stone steps climb to the garden.
Three restaurants and bars are within walking distance, and the riverside attractions are close by. It works as a holiday home or as a full-time home.
paragraphs.merdrignac-stone-cottage-newton: The property measures 120 m², with 3 bedrooms and 1 bathroom, on a plot of 265 m². Listed features: stone, terrace, garden. Located in Merdrignac, Brittany.
paragraphs.lacaze-timbered-house-60636342:
This is a timber-framed house (a colombage) in Lacaze, a medieval village listed as a Petite Cité de Caractère in the Tarn. It was the home of the arquebusier, the maker of early guns for the château, which you can see from the house.
The house has three levels and a dry cellar. The ground floor is a large open space that could be a workshop, a shop or a gallery. The first floor has already been refreshed and is ready to be fitted out. The three rooms on the second floor still need refreshing. Each floor has its own landing, so the house could easily become one flat per level.
Under the roof is a rare traditional frame, made by carpenters in the 16th or 17th century. A pellet stove and two open fireplaces heat the house, and there is a parking space in front. The upper floors need insulation, new windows and some modernising.
The village has a château, a museum, a gîte, a restaurant, a grocery, a post office and a bus. Toulouse is 1 hour 30 away, and Albi and Castres are 45 minutes.
paragraphs.champgeneteux-renovation-a44098:
The cottage is in a peaceful rural spot, down a quiet lane that it shares with only one other property, so it feels private.
The main house can be lived in today. It has a simple but practical layout and would benefit from modernising throughout, which leaves room to add value.
The plot has outbuildings, a garden and views over the countryside, and the agent sees potential for a gîte. The house has a wood burner.
paragraphs.pressignac-stone-cottage-a41100:
The cottage stands in the centre of a pretty hamlet, 2 km from the village of Pressignac, which has a restaurant, a post office, a bread depot and a grocery with local produce.
On the ground floor there is a large lounge and dining room, a fitted kitchen and a utility room. Upstairs are two bedrooms and a bathroom. The house has a small garden and an adjoining barn and garage.
The market towns of Rochechouart and Chabanais, with full amenities, are less than 9 km away. Lakes for walking, swimming, sailing, canoeing, fishing and horse riding, with restaurants and bars, are under 5 km away. Limoges airport is 45 km away.
paragraphs.la-chapelle-montbrandeix-stone-house-a29:
The house stands at the end of a small village, in a very green setting on the edge of the Dordogne. It has the charm of a cottage and is in good condition. The garden is large, and there is a garage and a big outbuilding (a dépendance).
Villages with all amenities, and historic monuments, are a few kilometres away.
paragraphs.thollet-farmhouse-bvi72280:
This longère, a long low farmhouse, stands in a small hamlet in the Vienne.
All the living space is on the ground floor: a well-equipped kitchen that opens onto the garden, a lounge, three bedrooms and a study or store room. There is a bathroom with a shower and a bath, and a separate toilet.
A large attic could become more living space, with the right permissions.
In the garden there is a terrace with a barbecue and covered seating. The listing also mentions a fireplace and a jacuzzi. Poitiers and Limoges airport are easy to reach.
paragraphs.saint-sebastien-cottage-a45393: The cottage stands in a lively little village that has some amenities, and it is in good condition. It has three bedrooms, a wood burner, a garden and private parking, and it is on mains drainage.
paragraphs.locarn-country-house-a45191:
The house is detached and quiet, with a low-maintenance garden. From one of the bedrooms you step onto a first-floor balcony terrace with wide views across the countryside.
Downstairs there is an entrance hall, a spacious fitted kitchen with a dining area, a cosy lounge with a log burner, a bathroom and a separate toilet. Upstairs there is a generous landing with room for a home office, and two double bedrooms.
The garage is attached to the house and leads to a small workshop and wood store, and then to the garden at the back. There is also a lawn at the front. The house has double glazing throughout and is heated by electric radiators and the log burner.
paragraphs.saint-ouen-la-thene-house-a39000:
The house stands in a calm and quiet hamlet, 3 km from the large village of Beauvais-sur-Matha, which has shops.
The current owners have looked after it well: it has double glazing, modern electrics and central heating.
Downstairs there is a large living room with a wood burner, a fitted kitchen with a dining area, a bathroom and a laundry area that leads to the boiler room and a workshop. The workshop could become a ground-floor bedroom. On the first floor are two bedrooms and a toilet with a hand basin. A separate floor has a third bedroom with its own shower room and a dressing room, and a mezzanine for storage.
Outside there is a manageable garden with a terrace and a 50 m² barn. The fosse septique (the private septic tank) will need updating.
Matha is 12 km away and Cognac 25 km. The Atlantic beaches are about an hour by car. The house is sold furnished.
paragraphs.saint-germain-de-confolens-house-a44033:
The house stands in the village of Saint-Germain-de-Confolens, where the Vienne and the Issoire meet, just minutes from the medieval town of Confolens.
Behind its traditional front, which dates from the 17th or 18th century, the living space is spread over three floors and keeps its period features. From the house you look towards the ruins of the Château de Saint-Germain-de-Confolens.
St Junien, Bellac and other market towns are less than an hour away. Limoges airport is 55 km away, Angoulême 67 km and Poitiers 72 km. It could be a home, a holiday home or a gîte.
paragraphs.exideuil-village-house-a44580: The property measures 189 m², with 5 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, on a plot of 669 m². Listed features: garden, outbuildings. Located in Exideuil-sur-Vienne, Nouvelle-Aquitaine.
paragraphs.azillanet-stone-house-a44962:
This stone house was built in 1874 and has been renovated to a high standard. The ground floor has a kitchen and dining room and a utility room.
On the first floor are a living room, which could also be a bedroom, and a spacious shower room. The second floor has a bedroom and a study, which could be a smaller bedroom.
At the top is a sun terrace with views over the landscape: the Corbières, the foothills of the Montagne Noire, the Pyrenees and the terracotta roofs of the village.
paragraphs.gourdon-stone-house-a43147:
This is an authentic stone house, partly built in the 15th century, in a small hamlet 4 km from the shops of Gourdon. The village is dominated by its church, built between the 12th and 16th centuries.
Inside there are exposed beams and stone, fireplaces and a mullioned window with a window seat.
On the ground floor is a large kitchen and dining room with a stove, and a few steps lead to the living room, which opens onto one of the terraces. Upstairs are three bedrooms and a bathroom. A convertible attic gives room to grow.
Outside there is a shaded garden and a recently built wooden terrace above small sheds, with open views of the countryside. The 19th-century bread oven is still in its original state. The house can be sold furnished if you wish.
paragraphs.gace-colombage-house-a39921:
This is a traditional timber-framed house (a colombage), tucked away in a peaceful hamlet near Gacé, in the Pays d'Auge in Normandy.
Inside there are three bedrooms, a wood burner and a modern pellet burner. A built-in cinema projector turns the living room into a home cinema.
Panoramic views over the surrounding countryside bring real rural calm. The house can be lived in straight away, and it also has renovation potential, so you could add living space to suit you.
paragraphs.la-roque-sur-ceze-village-house-a44763:
The house is in the heart of a perched medieval village in the Cèze valley, with panoramic views over the village and the countryside around it.
The village is known for its stone streets, river swimming spots, canoeing, hiking and nearby forests. It would make a good main home, a holiday home or a seasonal rental. The house has a wood burner and is on mains drainage.
paragraphs.riberac-stone-house-bvi77914:
The house stands at the end of a little row of cottages in a quiet hamlet, five minutes from Ribérac, which has all amenities, cafés, restaurants and a market every Friday.
It is attached to its neighbours, but still feels secluded, with private parking in front for two or three cars. The house can be lived in straight away, with an oil boiler and radiators throughout, and it is also a chance to renovate.
Two stone barns are attached to the house. They could be converted with planning permission. A separate workshop has views across the land and would suit a craftsman or an artist.
The garden and farmland together cover over 8 hectares.
paragraphs.saint-sulpice-house-bvi80970:
The house is in the centre of Saint-Sulpice-les-Feuilles, on the edge of the Haute-Vienne, but is set well back from the street and feels private. The village has bakers, bars, restaurants, shops and an English-speaking doctor, and the A20 gives good links to Paris, Limoges airport and the Channel ports.
A traditional door opens onto a tiled hallway, then the dining kitchen and a sitting room that keeps a marble fireplace. The house has air-source central heating.
Upstairs there is a modern shower room and three bright bedrooms. The main bedroom is huge. One of the other two opens through the other, so it could become a suite. A large attic could become more rooms, with permission.
Outside there is a sheltered courtyard for dining, a lawned garden, and a meadow that belongs to the local school next door. The furniture can be included, by negotiation, so it is a turn-key home.
paragraphs.chalais-stone-cottage-bvi86937: The property measures 87 m², with 2 bedrooms and 1 bathroom. Listed features: stone, fireplace, original features, garden. Located in Chalais, Nouvelle-Aquitaine.
paragraphs.la-trimouille-house-bvi85550:
The house is tucked away in a corner of La Trimouille, a lively river village with a cinema, cafés, a restaurant, a shop and a pharmacy on the doorstep.
The house is on one level. It has been recently renovated, with a new fitted kitchen and shower room, a connection to the mains sewer, modern electric radiators and fresh paint throughout. It keeps classic features: a chimney fire surround in the living room, parquet floors, high ceilings and traditional single-glazed windows.
Steps lead up to the living level. A bright living room has patio doors onto the balcony at the front. There is a second room that could be a bedroom, a dining room or an office, a bedroom, a shower room and a separate toilet. Below are a garage, a laundry room and a cellar.
The fenced garden has an extra outbuilding and a small studio room.
paragraphs.chateauponsac-stone-house-am5270: The house stands in the heart of the Limousin countryside, in the Haute-Vienne, close to the town of Châteauponsac and its shops. It is a stone house that has been fully renovated, with a wood stove, a large attached barn and a garden of 2,917 m². It is used today as a second home and is also let as a gîte for holidays.
paragraphs.chamberet-stone-house-cc4941: The property measures 85 m², with 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, on a plot of 1,835 m². Listed features: stone, fireplace, garden, garage, original features. Located in Chamberet, Nouvelle-Aquitaine.
paragraphs.valzergues-farmhouse-28262: The property measures 80 m², with 3 bedrooms and 1 bathroom, on a plot of 1,679 m². Listed features: stone, garden, outbuildings. Located in Valzergues, Occitanie.
paragraphs.lacourt-hamlet-house-32848:
The house stands in a peaceful hamlet at the end of a road, at an altitude of 600 m, in the commune of Lacourt, between Saint-Girons and Oust. It has been completely renovated, and no work is needed. It is semi-detached on one side, with an outbuilding.
The ground floor is a living room of 35 m² with a kitchenette, a landing and a toilet. Upstairs are two large bedrooms (14 m² and 20 m²) and a shower room with a toilet.
The attic is 28 m² and can be converted. There is a 20 m² terrace, and a separate plot of 380 m² lies 30 m from the house.
paragraphs.ginals-watermill-32445: The property measures 75 m², with 2 bedrooms and 1 bathroom, on a plot of 11,000 m². Listed features: historic, original features. Located in Ginals, Occitanie.
paragraphs.millac-hamlet-house-bvi87682:
This house stands in a hamlet and is in excellent condition. Inside, the floors are stone, the ceilings have wooden beams and the fireplace has a pellet burner. There are two bedrooms.
The plot has a barn with water and electricity, which could become extra living space with permission.
The nearest shop, bar and café are 5 km away. L'Isle-Jourdain is 13 km from the house, Confolens 21 km and Limoges airport 61 km.
paragraphs.ladapeyre-modernised-house-a36890:
The house is in the historic village of Ladapeyre, which has its own château. It has been fully modernised, is connected to mains drainage and has its own well.
The village is rural and very pretty, with an award-winning bakery, a bar and a post office, and open countryside all around. The lake at Châtelus-Malvaleix, with a bar and restaurant and a lifeguard in summer, is a 5-minute drive away.
It suits a family home, with or without income from letting, or a holiday home that needs very little upkeep.
paragraphs.siran-village-house-a42822:
This village house in Siran, in the heart of the Minervois, was newly renovated and is ready to move into. Exposed stone walls give the open ground floor its warmth. It has a kitchen with an induction hob and an electric oven, a living and dining area and a small private terrace.
Upstairs there are two bright double bedrooms and a spacious modern shower room. The basement has an extra room that could be a bar, a games room, storage or a hobby space.
The house is sold furnished. Shops and services are within 2 km and the airport is within 50 km. It works as a holiday home, a rental or an easy permanent home.
paragraphs.jumilhac-village-house-bvi85468:
This renovated house stands at the edge of the village of Jumilhac-le-Grand, within sight of the château, with views from every window. Inside there is a lounge, a kitchen and two double bedrooms, each with its original chimney, which could be reopened.
There is a cellar (a cave) for wine or storage, and a large attic that could be converted, with permission. At the back there is a small garden, with parking off the street.
The house is in good condition and on mains drainage. It is a short walk to the local shops.
paragraphs.avene-stone-house-a36741:
This stone house stands in a hamlet, surrounded by countryside, and keeps much of its old character.
Downstairs there is a large living room with a wood burner, a fitted kitchen and a shower room with a toilet. Upstairs there are three double bedrooms and a bathroom, and a staircase leads to a loft.
Outside there is a conservatory, a small paved garden and several small cellars with their own outside doors. The Avène thermal spa is a short drive away. It would suit a holiday home, a seasonal rental or a small family home.
paragraphs.saint-laurent-de-ceris-farmhouse-bvi8441:
This detached stone farmhouse stands at the edge of a Charente village and keeps several original features.
There are two double bedrooms, a sitting room with a kitchen, a dining room, a second reception room and a bathroom. It also has two large lofts, a cellar and a large attached barn. The garden surrounds the house and there is a driveway.
The village bar, bakery and shop are a short walk away. Confolens is nearby, and Limoges airport is about 40 minutes by car.
paragraphs.bouteilles-saint-sebastien-stone-house-a:
This stone house stands in a small, quiet hamlet, a short distance from the village of St Severin, which has shops, bars, restaurants, a medical centre and a school.
The ground floor has an entrance hall, a kitchen and dining area, a living area, two bedrooms and a shower room. A stone spiral staircase leads up to a large open-plan kitchen, dining and living room with a chimney. The third bedroom opens off it and has its own shower room.
More stairs lead to a roof terrace, recently re-sealed and tiled, with views across the rolling countryside.
There is a private parking space in front of the house. It has 160 m² of living space and is sold furnished.
paragraphs.lessac-hamlet-house-a48448:
This house stands in a peaceful hamlet, only 5 km from Confolens, a medieval town on the river with full amenities and services. It has 92 m² of living space.
The ground floor has an open-plan kitchen and living room, a dining room, a shower room and a toilet. Upstairs there are two bedrooms and an office.
A garden lies next to the house. The house can be lived in as it is. Limoges airport is 60 km away.
paragraphs.bonnefond-detached-house-a46567:
This detached house stands in a quiet hamlet in the Parc naturel régional de Millevaches. It has six rooms, three bedrooms and two bathrooms.
The living room has a powerful wood-burning stove. There is a fitted kitchen and a light-filled dining room, both looking onto the garden.
Upstairs, the large main bedroom has its own bathroom, a walk-in wardrobe and views over the countryside. The roof was replaced eight years ago.
The garden is over 800 m², borders the house and has wide views over the Plateau de Millevaches. The area is good for walks, cycling and fishing. The house is also listed as suitable for a gîte.
paragraphs.charras-stone-village-house-a39270:
This stone village house is in Charras. It has 85 m² of living space on three levels: a kitchen and dining room, a living room, a bedroom with its own bathroom and toilet, an office, a pantry with a toilet and a boiler room.
Two barns are attached to the house and offer room for more living space.
The garden next to the house has views over the countryside. The house is in good condition.
